content.text: Section 22 fully matches the preferred position, and Section 23 contains no substantive text that could create a broader access right.

input.quote: 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer's compliance with licence quantities no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, and in a manner that does not unreasonably disrupt Customer. An audit will be conducted off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality.
input.rationale: Section 22 is the only audit right binding us and it already meets the preferred position on every parameter: frequency capped at once per twelve months (22.1); at least thirty days' prior written notice; normal business hours with no unreasonable disruption; off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality (22.1); Vendor bears audit costs unless the audit establishes underpayment exceeding five percent, and then only reasonable costs plus the undisputed shortfall (22.2). Section 22.2 also expressly bars Vendor and its auditor from accessing Customer systems directly, Customer Data unrelated to usage, privileged material, or another supplier's confidential information, so the walk-away risks (unlimited/unannounced audits, remote system access) are absent. Section 22.3 further protects us by making findings Customer Confidential Information, limiting use to enforcement, requiring delivery of the final report, and treating payment of a shortfall as resolving the audited quantity issue. Section 23 (Records and Customer Assurance) contains only a heading with no substantive text, so it creates no broader inspection or access right, and a full-text search found no other audit, inspection, verification, or remote-access provisions elsewhere. No redline is warranted.
